title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment, not a failure of the camera system's recognition accuracy. A licensed user with legitimate credentials turned a query tool built for police work into a means of locating a private individual. The misuse ran across several state systems, which places it at the point where authorised access meets an absence of purpose limits on that access.

Catching it would have required auditing who queried whom and why, and treating repeated lookups of one person by one officer as a signal rather than routine traffic. The facts describe searches over two years, which suggests no such check fired during that period. Whether any logging or review process existed is not established.

The officer is accused, and a criminal complaint is not a finding of guilt. The internal affairs investigation and the Select Board hearing had not reached an outcome in the reporting, and the truth of the allegations is not established.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system multiple times in 2024 and 2025. The department said Rogers also used other state systems, including CJIS and CORI, to obtain information about her.

Stow police filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and opened an internal affairs investigation. He was placed on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has obtained a restraining order lasting at least a year. The police chief said a Select Board hearing will be held next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
